why: Two properties survived the search and one did not, so this is a split rather than a rubber stamp. SURVIVES (1) the obligation set is DERIVED from the tree, never declared: py_loc (codemap.py:293-300) sums tracked Python per directory and audit_prior_art (codemap.py:336-347) makes every directory at or above PRIOR_ART_LOC=300 owe a dated record unless a prefix in docs/prior-art/out-of-scope.txt says why not, and that exclusion file is printed on the PASS path too (codemap.py:407-411) so a suppression costs a visible line. Every expiry mechanism found inverts this direction: eslint-plugin-unicorn's expiring-todo-comments and todo-or-die expire a comment somebody remembered to write; Cortex Initiatives and OpsLevel Campaigns put a deadline on components somebody registered; a Thoughtworks radar holds rows somebody typed into a sheet. None of them can make code owe a record merely by growing past a line count, which is the one thing that makes this audit not a to-do list. SURVIVES (2) the two-way single-source rule: shadow_rows rejects a docs/dir-purpose.txt row sitting beside a directory that already documents itself, and stale_rows rejects a row that outlived its directory (codemap.py:254-256, 268-276). That is the exact opposite of the Backstage/Cortex/OpsLevel model, whose entire mechanism is a catalog-info.yaml sidecar restating the component's purpose next to the code -- the duplicate copy this check exists to forbid. DOES NOT SURVIVE: the prior-art record schema. PRIOR_ART_FIELDS (codemap.py:48-49) plus the truthiness loop at codemap.py:316-318 is a presence test over eight names. A JSON Schema validated by check-jsonschema would give types, a format/pattern on recheck_after, and a minItems on alternatives -- and the repo's own hard rule that a record needs at least three named alternatives is currently NOT machine-checked at all (an empty list is caught only because [] is falsy; a list of one passes). Worse, recheck_after is only ever date-parsed inside the `for component in owing` loop (codemap.py:356-361), so a record whose directory later falls below 300 lines or gets excluded keeps an unvalidated, unexpiring date forever. Keep the derivation, the purpose resolution and the registry hygiene; move the record shape to schemas/prior-art.schema.json and validate every file in docs/prior-art/, not just the ones currently owing.

alternatives.name: check-jsonschema (github.com/python-jsonschema/check-jsonschema, CLI + pre-commit hooks, built on the python jsonschema package)
alternatives.covers: THE ADOPT SLICE. Replaces read_records' hand-rolled required-field truthiness check (codemap.py:303-321) with a declarative JSON Schema: required fields, string types, a date pattern on recheck_after, minItems:3 on alternatives, and rejection of unknown keys. Validates EVERY file in docs/prior-art/ rather than only records whose component currently appears in the owing set, closing the stale-date hole at codemap.py:356-361. Docs at check-jsonschema.readthedocs.io show a generic hook taking --schemafile plus a files regex, which fits this directory exactly.
alternatives.gap: validates shape only. It cannot compute which directories owe a record, cannot compare a date against today and fail, cannot read out-of-scope.txt, and cannot detect a record naming a directory that no longer exists (codemap.py:365-368). Roughly 20 lines of codemap.py move to a schema file; the other ~500 stay.
alternatives.cost: a new pip dependency (check-jsonschema, which pulls jsonschema) in a currently stdlib-only tool, or a vendored jsonschema-free validator. Its pre-commit hook mode also fetches the hook repo on first use, which conflicts with the offline-CI habit unless pinned and cached. Licence not verified this session.
alternatives.maturity: docs page seen this session states version 0.37.4 and the pre-commit config in the repo pins rev 0.37.4; project lives under the python-jsonschema org. Release cadence and licence NOT independently verified.

alternatives.name: cog / cogapp (nedbatchelder.com/code/cog, nedbat/cog on GitHub, cogapp on PyPI)
alternatives.covers: the generate-then-verify mechanic. Cog runs embedded Python inside a text file and reinserts the output, and its --check option (confirmed on the Cog change history page) reports whether a file WOULD change, which is precisely what cmd_write plus the drifted comparison do (codemap.py:375-383, 240-260).
alternatives.gap: cog does not write the generator, it only hosts it -- inventory/resolve/render (codemap.py:131-226) is the actual code and would be pasted verbatim into a cog block. Adopting it would also put executable Python inside docs/CODEBASE-MAP.md, a 362-row generated table that is meant to be read and diffed, and cog's --check reports file-level 'would change' with no equivalent of problems()' named missing_rows/extra_rows/changed_rows (codemap.py:281-289). It has nothing for the prior-art half. Note the honest alternative to BOTH: `codemap.py write && git diff --exit-code -- docs/CODEBASE-MAP.md` already gives a better diff than the custom comparison for free.
alternatives.cost: one pip dependency; small. But it would replace roughly 40 lines while inverting who owns the file.
alternatives.maturity: active. A 2026 practitioner post (alexwlchan.net, cog-in-my-caddy) and a 3.6.0 docs page were both seen this session; exact latest release NOT verified.

alternatives.name: terraform-docs (terraform-docs.io) and helm-docs
alternatives.covers: the canonical, mature instance of this whole pattern: read structured source, render a documentation block, and fail the build in --check mode when the committed copy differs. Search results this session confirm the pre-commit integration exists precisely so a commit fails when generated docs drift.
alternatives.gap: both are domain-locked parsers. terraform-docs reads .tf variable/output/provider blocks; helm-docs reads Chart.yaml and values.yaml. Neither can resolve a purpose out of a heterogeneous set of SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, README.md, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md with a precedence order (codemap.py:43, 131-143), neither has any notion of a directory that documents itself nowhere (the UNDOCUMENTED count that is the entire point of the header line at codemap.py:211-212), and neither has a registry, a shadow rule, or a prior-art concept.
alternatives.cost: free Go binaries, easy install; but adopting either means the repo would have to become a Terraform module or Helm chart, which is not a trade, it is a category error.
alternatives.maturity: both long-established and widely used per the practitioner guides found; release cadence NOT verified this session.

alternatives.name: Backstage software catalog (backstage.io) with catalog-info.yaml and `backstage-cli repo lint` in CI
alternatives.covers: the strongest conceptual match for the map half: a per-component YAML descriptor carrying description/owner/lifecycle, harvested into a browsable catalog, with the documented practice (confirmed in search results) of adding a CI check that rejects PRs introducing an invalid or ownerless catalog file. That is 'every unit of this repo must state what it is for, enforced in CI'.
alternatives.gap: the mechanism is a sidecar file per component that RESTATES the purpose next to code that often already states it -- which is exactly what shadow_rows fails the build over (codemap.py:255-256, 272-276). Backstage's unit is a Component/System/API registered by a human, not the 362 directories git already knows about, so nothing is derived and a new directory is simply absent rather than failing. And Backstage is a Node application with a backend and a database, not a script a Stop hook can run offline.
alternatives.cost: a running Backstage instance (Node server plus a database) or a hosted equivalent; disproportionate for a single-maintainer stdlib-Python repo. Free and open source; exact licence NOT verified this session.
alternatives.maturity: CNCF-scale project, actively documented in 2026 pages fetched by search; I did NOT read Backstage source or verify what repo lint actually enforces beyond the third-party summaries returned.

alternatives.name: Cortex Initiatives (cortex.io) and OpsLevel Campaigns (opslevel.com)
alternatives.covers: the closest commercial match for the prior-art half's shape: scorecard rules over a component catalog plus a deadline. Cortex's own post 'Cortex Initiatives: When scorecards need a deadline' describes carving a scorecard slice, assigning a due date, and sending automated nudges 7 days and 1 day before; its worked example is literally 'ensure all software has a README attached by next month', which is one of this component's two checks. OpsLevel Campaigns is the same idea with notifications and reporting.
alternatives.gap: the deadline attaches to a REMEDIATION drive across components, not to the validity of an individual evidence record. There is no equivalent of 'this specific build-vs-buy record was written on 2026-07-29 and stops counting as evidence on 2026-10-27, at which point the check fails again' (codemap.py:356-364). The catalog is again human-registered per service, so nothing is derived from line counts, and the unit is a service or repo, not one of 362 directories. Both are hosted SaaS: no offline run, no local Stop hook, and the check lives outside the repo it audits.
alternatives.cost: commercial SaaS, seat-priced. I did NOT verify current pricing, free-tier availability, or whether either offers a self-hosted or CLI-only mode. For a one-person personal harness the cost is almost certainly disqualifying, but that is inference, not a verified quote.
alternatives.maturity: both are established vendors in the internal-developer-portal category per the comparison pages found; feature claims above come from vendor marketing pages and were NOT verified against a running instance.

alternatives.name: eslint-plugin-unicorn `expiring-todo-comments` (sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn), plus todo-or-die (davidpdrsn/todo-or-die, Rust), the todo_or_die Ruby gem, andyw8/do_by, and the expiring-todo-comments-action on GitHub Marketplace
alternatives.covers: the expiry primitive, and more richly than ours. Its rule doc confirms ISO YYYY-MM-DD expiry (behind checkDates), plus expiry on `engine:node@>=8`, on a package version `bar-package@>=2`, on a peer dep, or on a package being added or removed, with multiple conditions comma-joined. todo-or-die adds compile-time expiry on 'this GitHub issue closed' and 'this crate reached version X'. A dependency-version trigger would be a genuine upgrade to a build-vs-buy record: 'reopen this when the alternative ships version N'.
alternatives.gap: every one of them expires a comment or macro a human chose to write. There is no derived obligation: a 3302-line directory with no TODO in it owes nothing, which is the precise failure mode audit_prior_art was built to prevent (module docstring, codemap.py:17-21: 'the set of components that owe a record is derived from line count, not from a list, so code cannot be born exempt'). They also expire nothing outside source comments -- a JSON evidence record in docs/ is invisible to all of them -- and unicorn is JS-only in a stdlib-Python repo.
alternatives.cost: eslint plus the plugin (npm) for a repo with no JS toolchain; todo-or-die is Rust-only. Free.
alternatives.maturity: unicorn is long-established and the rule doc was read this session; todo-or-die's docs.rs page and its Hacker News thread were seen. Current release versions of any of them NOT verified.

alternatives.name: interrogate (interrogate.readthedocs.io) and docstr_coverage (HunterMcGushion/docstr_coverage)
alternatives.covers: the language-native form of 'measure how much of this codebase states its purpose and fail below a threshold'. interrogate reports which modules, classes, functions and methods have docstrings and fails CI under --fail-under, and ships a pre-commit hook. That is the same shape as render()'s header line 'N directories, M tracked files, K without a stated purpose' (codemap.py:211-212).
alternatives.gap: the unit is a Python object, not a directory, and the source of truth is a docstring, not a README/SKILL.md/AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md fallback chain. It cannot cover a directory of markdown skills or YAML workflows, which is most of this repo. It has no generated artifact to compare against, so no drift check; no registry, no shadow/stale rules, and it is a percentage-threshold tool where this check is absolute (any UNDOCUMENTED directory fails, codemap.py:264-267).
alternatives.cost: one pip dependency; genuinely light. It just answers a different question.
alternatives.maturity: docs page seen this session states v1.7.0; actively used in the Python ecosystem per the PyAnsys and pre-commit guides found. Latest release date NOT verified.

alternatives.name: Repomix (repomix.com, yamadashy/repomix) and Gitingest (gitingest.com)
alternatives.covers: generating a machine-readable map of a repository for an LLM, which is who actually reads docs/CODEBASE-MAP.md. Both are git-aware (respect .gitignore), both emit a directory tree plus content, Repomix adds token counts, Secretlint scanning, and a --compress mode that uses Tree-sitter to keep structure while dropping bodies.
alternatives.gap: they emit a throwaway pack for one prompt, not a committed artifact with a drift check -- there is no --check, no comparison against a previous output, and no failure mode. They also carry no notion of a directory's stated PURPOSE: they ship the content and let the model infer, whereas resolve() (codemap.py:131-143) requires a human-authored sentence and names the file it came from in the `from` column, so a reader can tell a maintained purpose from a guessed one. Neither has a registry or a prior-art half. Repomix's output would also be enormous next to a 362-row table.
alternatives.cost: Repomix is npm/npx (Node); Gitingest is a hosted site plus a browser extension, i.e. it would send repository contents to a third party, which is disqualifying here on its own. Licences NOT verified.
alternatives.maturity: Repomix is prominent and actively developed per its site and GitHub topic pages seen this session; star counts and release cadence NOT verified.

alternatives.name: Thoughtworks Build Your Own Radar (thoughtworks.com/radar/byor) and the tech-radar practice generally
alternatives.covers: the named industry practice behind the prior-art half: classify each technology as adopt/trial/assess/hold and revisit the whole set on a cadence (the Thoughtworks guidance found says a couple of times a year, which is roughly this record's 90-day recheck_after).
alternatives.gap: BYOR is a visualisation: it reads a Google Sheet or hosted CSV/JSON with columns name/ring/quadrant/isNew/description and draws an HTML5 canvas. Nothing derives entries from the codebase, nothing expires, nothing exits non-zero, and it classifies technologies the org might use rather than recording why a specific 520-line directory was written instead of adopting one. The cadence is a meeting, not a check.
alternatives.cost: free and self-hostable; but it produces a picture, not a gate.
alternatives.maturity: long-established practice (Neal Ford's 2013 post plus current Thoughtworks pages found); tool repo activity NOT verified.

alternatives.name: log4brains (thomvaill/log4brains) and adr-tools, the ADR ecosystem
alternatives.covers: dated decision records in the repo, docs-as-code, with a lifecycle status (proposed/accepted/superseded) and a published static site. This repo already has 15 ADRs under docs/adr, so the format is not foreign to it.
alternatives.gap: an ADR's status changes when a human writes a superseding ADR. There is no expiry date that fires by itself, no required-field validation, and above all no derived set of decisions that MUST exist -- an undocumented decision is simply an ADR nobody wrote. Search this session surfaced organisations hand-writing 'last reviewed on X, review again by Y' into ADR bodies, which confirms the need and confirms that no tool enforces it.
alternatives.cost: log4brains is a Node CLI plus static-site generator; adr-tools is shell. Light, but they solve authoring and publishing, not enforcement.
alternatives.maturity: adr-tools and log4brains both appear in current (2026) ADR guides found this session; neither repo's activity was checked directly.

what_ours_does: One file, codemap.py (520 lines), four verbs, two jobs that share one failure mode: a fact written into a document once and trusted forever (module docstring, codemap.py:2-6). MAP JOB. tracked() (codemap.py:146-167) runs `git ls-files -z` with a literal argv and no shell, decoding NUL-separated records so a Hebrew directory name arrives as a path instead of a C-quoted string that matches no registry row -- the docstring records that 5 of 194 then-undocumented directories were that bug. inventory() (170-185) derives every directory implied by a tracked path plus its direct file count. resolve() (131-143) finds each directory's purpose in precedence order: SKILL.md YAML frontmatter `description:` including folded-scalar forms (from_frontmatter, 86-106), else the first prose line of SKILL.md/README.md/AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (first_prose, 109-115), else a `path | purpose` row in docs/dir-purpose.txt (read_registry, 118-128), else UNDOCUMENTED. render() (197-226) emits docs/CODEBASE-MAP.md grouped by top-level area with a `from` column naming the source of each purpose, escaping any pipe as | rather than backslash (cell, 190-194, with a comment explaining that a backslash-escaped pipe is still a pipe) and eliding at 180 chars; it deliberately carries no timestamp, no commit sha and no line counts, because each of those would guarantee drift on every commit and train the reader to ignore the check (207-209). evaluate()/problems() (240-290) regenerate, compare the whole string against the file on disk, and report four fault classes by name: undocumented directories, stale_rows (a registry row whose directory is gone), shadow_rows (a registry row beside a directory that already documents itself -- the anti-duplication rule), and drift, where the message names the specific missing/extra/changed rows rather than just saying 'drifted' (281-289). PRIOR-ART JOB. py_loc() (293-300) sums tracked Python lines per directory; audit_prior_art() (336-370) makes every directory at or above 300 lines owe a record in docs/prior-art/, subtracting only prefixes listed with a reason in out-of-scope.txt (read_scope, 324-333), then requires eight non-empty fields (read_records, 303-321), an ISO recheck_after not in the past, and that no record names a directory absent from the repository. cmd_prior_art (402-418) prints every exclusion on the PASS path too, on the stated grounds that an exclusion nobody sees is a disabled check. SELFTEST. cmd_selftest (421-505, added 2026-07-27 because this module owned two required gate domains with nothing to falsify them) plants one defect per guarantee: pipe escaping, elision, render/map_rows round-trip parseability, the undocumented count in the header, one message per fault class, drift naming the row, and -- after mutation testing found the hole -- a missing map saying 'is missing.' and specifically NOT the drift wording (496-501). Verified locally: 12/12 pass.
strongest_counterargument: This file is two days old (one commit, 8d40794) and the audit that demands its record is written into the same file, so the component is grading its own homework twice over: codemap.py both defines what owes a prior-art record and is one of the things owing one, and there is no independent process that would notice if PRIOR_ART_LOC were quietly raised from 300 to 600 and half the obligations vanished -- out-of-scope.txt at least costs a printed line, but the threshold constant costs nothing and is not printed anywhere. Against the verdict specifically: the split I declared is the small half. The honest larger claim is that the MAP half is mostly a general pattern already solved -- generate, then `git diff --exit-code` -- and that evaluate()'s 20-line map_rows regex parser plus missing/extra/changed sets (codemap.py:231-237, 249-252) exists only to print a nicer message than git diff already prints in colour, with the added risk that if render()'s row format ever changes the parser silently matches nothing and reports zero named rows while still failing on the whole-string comparison. Strip that and the drift check is four lines of shell. What is left that is genuinely unique is smaller than 520 lines: the SELF_DOC precedence chain, the shadow/stale registry rules, py_loc plus the LOC-derived obligation set, and the recheck_after expiry -- call it 150 lines of idea inside 520 lines of code. And on the third-party side I am arguing from documentation, not from use: I did not install cog, check-jsonschema, terraform-docs, Backstage or Repomix, so every 'gap' above is a claim about what the docs say a tool does not do, and a docs-based absence is the weakest kind of evidence this repo accepts. A future session that actually runs check-jsonschema against docs/prior-art/*.json and finds it catches more real defects than read_records ever has should widen the split, not narrow it.
